newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila seeks meeting with Malaysia over hotel row.
newsitem.headline: Manila seeks meeting with Malaysia over hotel row.

text.p: The Philippine Foreign Secretary said on Thursday he would meet his Malaysian counterpart next week in a bid to defuse tensions after a court ruled the historic Manila Hotel could not be sold to a Malaysian firm.
The Supreme Court ruled on Monday that the government-owned hotel was a national treasure and could not be sold to a foreign entity.
The informal talks with Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi will take place on the sidelines of the ASEAN-European Union ministers meeting in Singapore, Domingo Siazon told reporters.
"It will be difficult to explain. We are embarrassed," Siazon said. "It's good we are able to say that the Supreme Court is independent, that it cannot really be influenced."

The court stopped the government from selling the property to Renong Bhd, which had won the 1995 bidding for the hotel, and instructed it to award the contract to the local Manila Prince Hotel Corp in keeping with a "Filipino First" policy.
The court initially issued a temporary restraining order suspending implementation of the bidding results after Renong was declared the winner.
Siazon said there were complaints from the Malaysians even then, but he did not specify who voiced them.
"In a globalised economy, you can no longer argue that way," Siazon said, referring to arguments that the Manila Hotel was part of national patrimony.
